rows.proposition: Immortality, rebirth and liberation are distinct relations: survival does not by itself entail another embodiment, and Buddhist rebirth does not require a substantial immortal soul.
Competing substance, embodied-person, bundle and causal-continuity models supply different answers to who or what persists through death and rebirth.
Plato and several Indian schools defend enduring soul models, while Kantian and body-brain objections challenge whether survival has been demonstrated.

source_anchor.heading: 1.1 Arguments for immortality and their limits

rows.proposition: Simplicity, identity, moral-order, desire and religious-experience arguments support immortality only with contestable premises and do not independently establish rebirth.

destinations.anchor: 1.1 Arguments for immortality and their limits

rows.proposition: Rebirth extends karmic continuity across lives; substantialist schools add a transmigrating bearer, whereas Buddhism explains renewed becoming without a permanent self.
Liberation names non-identical goals across Advaita, Viśiṣṭādvaita, Nyāya, Sāṃkhya-Yoga, Jainism, Buddhism and Western traditions.
The foundational facts connect Gītā imagery, Platonic recollection, Buddhist causal continuity, jīvanmukti and Nyāya apavarga to exam-ready distinctions.
The drill bank routes each major doctrine to a specific evaluative demand rather than treating immortality, rebirth and liberation as interchangeable.

source_anchor.heading: 5A. LIBERATION PARITY BENCH — the six terms must never be merged ⚠️

rows.proposition: Mokṣa, apavarga, kaivalya, Jain liberation, nirvāṇa and resurrection differ over what ends, what remains and whether consciousness persists.

destinations.anchor: 5A. LIBERATION PARITY BENCH — the six terms must never be merged ⚠️

source_anchor.heading: 6.1 — "Is immortality of the soul a necessary condition for rebirth? (w.r.t. Buddhism)" (2022, 10m)

rows.proposition: Buddhism defeats necessity, while substantial-soul immortality remains insufficient by itself because rebirth also requires a transmigration or re-embodiment account.
rows.delta_note: The destination preserves the canonical question while correcting the mistaken inference from immortality alone to rebirth.

destinations.anchor: 6.1 — "Is immortality of the soul a necessary condition for rebirth? (w.r.t. Buddhism)" (2022, 10m)

rows.proposition: Advaita presents jīvanmukti as liberation through knowledge while embodied life continues under prārabdha karma until videhamukti.

source_anchor.heading: 6.3 — "Evaluate the concept of Bhakti (Devotion) as a pathway to attain liberation." (2018, 15m)

rows.proposition: Bhakti traditions differ over devotion, surrender, grace and whether bhakti directly liberates or prepares the aspirant for knowledge.

destinations.anchor: 6.3 — "Evaluate the concept of Bhakti (Devotion) as a pathway to attain liberation." (2018, 15m)

source_anchor.heading: 6.4 — "Are Knowledge, Action and Devotion the means to liberation in Indian tradition?" (2020, 15m)

rows.proposition: Indian schools classify knowledge, action and devotion as direct, preparatory, sequential or grace-dependent means according to their account of bondage.

destinations.anchor: 6.4 — "Are Knowledge, Action and Devotion the means to liberation in Indian tradition?" (2020, 15m)

rows.proposition: Karma supplies moral causation, rebirth supplies the cross-life field, and reincarnation adds the school-specific claim of a substantial bearer entering another body.
The advanced dossiers deepen the canonical doctrines through arguments, presuppositions, distinctions, examples and objection-reply pairs.
Plato's cyclical, recollection, affinity and Form-of-Life arguments require separate evaluation because pre-existence and resemblance to Forms do not automatically prove post-mortem survival.
Vedāntic systems connect an enduring self with karmic embodiment but diverge sharply between Advaitic non-dual realization and Viśiṣṭādvaitic personal communion.

source_anchor.heading: 8.3 Buddhist rebirth without an immortal soul

rows.proposition: Dependent origination and neither-same-nor-different continuity explain karmic rebirth without an unchanging owner of the aggregates.

destinations.anchor: 8.3 Buddhist rebirth without an immortal soul

rows.proposition: Jainism treats jīva as enduring, karma as material bondage, and liberation as the perfected soul's release through stopping and shedding karmic influx.
Nyāya apavarga as cessation without liberated consciousness contrasts with Advaita jīvanmukti as self-luminous freedom while living.

source_anchor.heading: 8.6 Bhakti as a path to liberation (2018 Q7(c) owner-module)

rows.proposition: Bhakti theories compare disciplined remembrance, surrender, grace, divine dependence and the tension between dualistic love and non-dual liberation.

destinations.anchor: 8.6 Bhakti as a path to liberation (2018 Q7(c) owner-module)

source_anchor.heading: 8.7 Jñāna, karma and bhakti — how the three means are related (2020 Q8(c) owner-module)

rows.proposition: The three means converge in transforming agency but diverge over whether liberation is produced, received or disclosed by removing ignorance.

destinations.anchor: 8.7 Jñāna, karma and bhakti — how the three means are related (2020 Q8(c) owner-module)

source_anchor.heading: 8.8 Resurrection versus rebirth — and rebirth versus reincarnation

rows.proposition: Resurrection reconstitutes the embodied person after one life, rebirth is the wider cross-life continuity category, and reincarnation presupposes a substantial transmigrant.

destinations.anchor: 8.8 Resurrection versus rebirth — and rebirth versus reincarnation

source_anchor.heading: 8.9 Sāṃkhya and Yoga: *kaivalya*, and how it differs from every other liberation

rows.proposition: Sāṃkhya-Yoga kaivalya isolates puruṣa from prakṛti and must not be confused with Brahman-identity, divine communion, omniscience or Buddhist cessation.

destinations.anchor: 8.9 Sāṃkhya and Yoga: *kaivalya*, and how it differs from every other liberation

rows.proposition: The comparative debates test soul versus no-self continuity, identity versus communion, conscious versus non-conscious release, and natural immortality versus resurrection.
Memory, verification, bodily dependence, justice and identity objections each require a doctrine-specific reply rather than a generic appeal to faith.
The trap list prevents conflating rebirth with reincarnation, nirvāṇa with annihilation, apavarga with bliss, kaivalya with kevala and liberation with merger.
The keyword bank supplies precise terms and formulations for continuity, bondage, release, identity and school-specific mechanisms.
The depth delta adds the doctrine, thinker and comparison material demanded by the verified PYQ corpus beyond a minimal syllabus outline.
The routing table assigns each verified question to this owner, a supporting module or an explicit boundary so ownership remains auditable.
Answer architecture scales argument density, comparison and evaluation to the locked 10-, 15- and 20-mark formats.
A 10-mark response uses a direct definition, compact doctrinal contrast, one objection and a qualified conclusion within 150 to 200 words.
A 15-mark response develops two or three doctrinal axes, evaluation and a reasoned verdict within 250 to 300 words.
A 20-mark response integrates conceptual distinctions, multiple traditions, objections, replies and a defended synthesis within 340 to 400 words.
The directive decoder distinguishes descriptive, comparative and critical tasks so the answer's operations match the command word.
The verdict ladder replaces absolute conclusions with calibrated judgments about logical possibility, doctrinal dependence and evidential strength.
